repositoryDescription: Early-stage, local-first Windows piano sight-reading practice for user-provided MusicXML/MXL scores, with optional MIDI-controller input.

responses.question: Why is the repository eligible?
responses.answer: Cadenza is not yet eligible because the public repository has no project LICENSE. Once the maintainer approves and merges GPL-3.0, it will be an early-stage, local-first Windows piano sight-reading tool for user-owned MusicXML/MXL scores, with original fixtures, contributor governance, and clean-clone validation. The maintainer will review every AI-assisted change.

responses.question: How would API credits be used?
responses.answer: API credits would support maintainer-reviewed work on reduced MusicXML compatibility cases, repeat/volta regressions, Windows accessibility, documentation, and contributor issue/PR triage. Credits would also help generate and test bounded malformed-input cases. They would not fund a song catalogue or autonomous merges; the maintainer remains responsible for review, validation, and release decisions.

responses.question: Why does the project need Codex Security?
responses.answer: Cadenza processes untrusted MusicXML/MXL and MIDI files, stores local score/history data, bridges .NET to a WebView2 renderer, and accepts optional WinMM input. Codex Security could model these boundaries, validate archive, parser, path, and bridge flaws, and propose minimal regression-backed patches. Findings and patches would require maintainer review; no production-security claim is made.

responses.question: Is there anything else OpenAI should consider?
responses.answer: Cadenza is Windows-first, pre-release, incomplete, and not significantly adopted. Automated validation covers original fixtures without MIDI or audio hardware; real devices, WebView2 UI, audio, and accessibility still need manual checks. The application should not be submitted until GPL-3.0 is approved and merged. The maintainer remains responsible for human review and merge decisions.
